0.title: 2027 Season Preview: A Clean Slate in the ACC
0.subtitle: Fifteen teams, zero losses, and one trophy — the dynasty league kicks off Week 0
0.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Season Outlook
sections.content: A new season is finally here. Every team in the conference sits at 0-0, and until the games kick off, everyone can dream about hoisting the ACC Championship trophy. Clemson opens the season at the top of the preseason Dynasty Poll and enters as the team to beat, but Miami and Louisville both have legitimate title aspirations. With a 15-week road to the conference championship, the margin for error is thin — early stumbles in September have a way of haunting teams come November.

sections.heading: Teams to Watch
sections.content: Clemson carries the preseason #1 tag and the pressure that comes with it. Miami boasts the most explosive offense on paper, while Louisville's balanced roster makes the Cardinals a trendy title pick. Don't sleep on the middle of the pack either — NC State, Duke, and Pittsburgh all cracked the preseason Top 25, and Georgia Tech and Virginia Tech are lurking just behind them. At the bottom, Wake Forest and Stanford are looking to prove the projections wrong.

sections.heading: Schedule on the Way
sections.content: The Week 0 slate hasn't been set just yet — the league is still working through the transfer portal, and the full schedule will be generated in-game once rosters are locked. Check the Schedule page once matchups are announced to see who opens the season against whom. In the meantime, the preseason Dynasty Poll is live and the standings are wiped clean — all fifteen teams start from zero.

1.title: Week 1: Arkansas State Stuns Virginia as the ACC Splits Opening Weekend
1.subtitle: A 38–0 shutout in Charlottesville, a .500 opening slate, and a brand-new No. 1 — the 2027 season wasted no time getting weird
1.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Opening Weekend Recap
sections.content: The ACC's opening slate ended in a perfect split — six wins, six losses — and almost none of it went according to script. Louisville looked the sharpest of anyone, handling Charlotte 35–13 for the conference's biggest win of the weekend. Duke, Wake Forest, Pittsburgh, Syracuse, and Stanford all took care of business at home, with the Cardinal surviving a 32–29 scare from Air Force. But the other half of the conference has some soul-searching to do: Georgia Tech managed just a field goal in a 23–3 home loss to Ohio, NC State fell flat against Louisiana, and Boston College, California, and North Carolina all dropped home games they were expected to win. Clemson, Miami, and Virginia Tech sat out the opening weekend and watched the chaos from the couch.

sections.heading: Upset of the Week: Arkansas State 38, Virginia 0
sections.content: There are losses, and then there's whatever happened in Charlottesville. Virginia — ranked No. 19 in the country — didn't just lose to Arkansas State, they got shut out 38–0 at home in the worst opening-week result anyone in this league can remember. The Cavaliers somehow clung to their No. 19 ranking in this week's poll, but nobody's buying it until they show signs of life. Honorable mention to Georgia Southern, who walked into Chapel Hill and beat North Carolina 38–35.

sections.heading: Poll Shakeup: A New No. 1
sections.content: The voters hit the reset button. LSU rocketed from No. 14 all the way to the top spot without playing a down, while preseason No. 1 Clemson tumbled out of the Top 25 entirely — the Tigers will get their first chance to answer when they finally take the field. The ACC places four teams in the new poll: Miami climbs to No. 2, Pittsburgh jumps nine spots to No. 11, Wake Forest debuts at No. 12 after dispatching San Diego State, and Virginia hangs on at No. 19 by a thread. Louisville's 22-point win somehow wasn't enough to crack the list — file that one under motivation.

sections.heading: Week 1 Games to Watch
sections.content: The marquee matchup is obvious: No. 12 Wake Forest travels to Acrisure Stadium to face No. 11 Pittsburgh in a top-15, 1-0 vs. 1-0 conference clash that will hand someone an early inside track in the ACC race. Elsewhere, Virginia Tech finally opens its season at home against Liberty (Saturday, 3:30 PM ET at Lane Stadium), North Carolina gets a shot at redemption against Texas State, and California tries to wash out the Buffalo loss against UL Monroe. Clemson and Miami remain idle — the wait for the preseason heavyweights continues.

2.title: Week 2: Wake Forest Rises to the Top of the ACC
2.subtitle: The Demon Deacons are 2–0, they knocked off Pitt on the road, and they're now the conference's highest-ranked team — while Miami free-falls and the ACC treads water at 6–6 again
2.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 1 Recap
sections.content: Wake Forest is the story of the weekend. The Demon Deacons walked into Acrisure Stadium, knocked off No. 20 Pittsburgh 26–16 in the ACC's only conference game, and moved to 2–0 — the lone league team with a win that actually counts in the standings. They now headline a four-team pack of unbeatens alongside Stanford, Louisville, and Duke. For the second straight weekend the conference landed right on the .500 line at 6–6 against non-conference foes: Louisville (42–3 over Missouri State) and NC State (45–3 over Kent State) posted the most lopsided wins, while Syracuse got tripped up at home by Sam Houston 28–20, Liberty rolled Virginia Tech 41–25, Ball State stunned Georgia Tech 20–13, and Fresno State handled Virginia 30–12. And Clemson? Still waiting to play its first snap of 2027.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Wake Forest
sections.content: Nobody else in the ACC can say what the Demon Deacons can: 2–0, a conference win already in the pocket, and a road takedown of a ranked team. Wake climbed to No. 11 in the new poll — the highest-ranked team in the league — and did it the hard way, silencing Acrisure Stadium against a Pittsburgh squad that entered the week in the Top 15. If there's an early front-runner in the ACC race, it's wearing old gold and black.

sections.heading: Poll Check: Miami's Free-Fall
sections.content: While Wake was rising, Miami was in free-fall. Two weeks ago the Hurricanes sat at No. 2 in the country; now they're No. 13 after a 22–13 loss to No. 8 Utah — an 11-spot tumble. Pittsburgh slid from No. 11 to No. 20 after the Wake Forest defeat, and Virginia dropped out of the Top 25 entirely, sitting at 0–2 and outscored 68–12 across two games. That leaves the ACC with just three ranked teams: Wake Forest (11), Miami (13), and Pittsburgh (20).

sections.heading: Week 2 Games to Watch
sections.content: The one that matters most: NC State travels to California in the week's lone ACC conference clash, a 1–1 vs. 1–1 tilt that hands the winner an early tiebreaker. Wake Forest hosts Utah State trying to stay unbeaten and ranked, Louisville and Duke look to keep rolling against Nevada and Bowling Green, and Virginia Tech hits the road at Texas State to chase its first win. Stanford is on a bye. Miami sits idle — and yes, Clemson's debut is still on hold.

3.title: Week 3: Clemson Crashes the Party as Conference Play Arrives
3.subtitle: The Tigers finally debut with a 62–7 haymaker, Wake Forest keeps rolling into the national top 10, and the ACC opens its first real week of league games
3.author: Tdoghawks23

sections.heading: Week 2 Recap
sections.content: Clemson has entered the chat. After sitting out the first two weekends, the Tigers made their 2027 debut count, burying Arizona 62–7 for the most lopsided result the ACC has posted all year. They weren't the only ones feasting: Duke hung 58 on Bowling Green, Louisville handled Nevada 29–17, and Wake Forest stayed perfect with a 21–10 win over Utah State. In the conference's lone league game, California went to work on NC State 25–12 to grab an early tiebreaker in the standings, and Syracuse shook off its Week 1 stumble with a clean 20–0 shutout of Delaware. The bottom of the league, though, had a miserable Saturday: Pittsburgh got upset at home by Colorado State 28–27, North Carolina couldn't hold off Coastal Carolina in a 41–31 track meet, Boston College fell to Troy to drop to 0–3, Georgia Tech lost to FCS Southeast 27–24 for an ugly FCS defeat, Virginia dropped an overtime heartbreaker to Cincinnati 32–26, and Virginia Tech let one slip at Texas State 18–14.

sections.heading: Team of the Week: Wake Forest
sections.content: The Demon Deacons just keep answering the bell. At 3–0 with a conference win already banked, Wake is the only unbeaten in the ACC that also owns a league victory, and the voters rewarded them — Wake climbed to No. 9 in the new poll, cracking the national top 10 and standing alone as the highest-ranked team in the conference. Clemson's blowout will grab the headlines, but until someone knocks the Deacons off, the road to the ACC race still runs through Winston-Salem.

sections.heading: Poll Check: Three Ranked, and a New No. 1
sections.content: The ACC now has three teams in the poll for the first time this season. Wake Forest leads the way at No. 9, Miami quietly climbed back to No. 11 despite sitting idle at 0–1 as the teams around them stumbled, and Louisville finally broke through, debuting at No. 24 on the strength of a 3–0 start. The bad news came out of Pittsburgh: the Panthers tumbled out of the Top 25 entirely after the Colorado State upset. Nationally, the top of the board reshuffled — Oklahoma jumped to No. 1, bumping LSU to No. 2 and Ohio State to No. 3.

sections.heading: Week 3 Games to Watch
sections.content: Conference play arrives in force — six of the eight games on the slate are league matchups. The one circled on our calendar: Syracuse hosts Clemson at the JMA Wireless Dome, and the Orange get the unenviable job of trying to cool off a Tigers team fresh off a 55-point debut. Elsewhere, No. 24 Louisville travels to Stanford in a battle of unbeatens, Duke hosts NC State with both teams looking to prove their fast start is real, and North Carolina welcomes Pittsburgh in a matchup of teams desperate to steady the ship. Down at the bottom, Georgia Tech and Boston College meet in a 0–3 vs. 0–3 scrap where somebody finally gets in the win column. Wake Forest (vs. UNLV) and Virginia Tech (vs. Maryland) round out the week in non-conference play.
